events-men.note: I counted 20 men's rows on the Wikipedia list (100 m to decathlon) under the stated definition: individual Olympic events, no relays, no race walks. The count follows from that definition; no source states it.

events-women.note: I counted 20 women's rows (100 m to heptathlon) under the same definition. The marathon is counted once, with the mixed-race record.

records-pre-1990.note: My recount gives 9: men's hammer (1986) plus the 8 women's records. The men's long jump (1991) and high jump (1993) are after 1990. Unchanged if the pending 27 Aug 2026 marks are counted.

records-pre-1990-women.note: My recount gives 8: W800 1983, W400 1985, SP 1987, and from 1988 the 100, 200, long jump, discus and heptathlon.

records-since-2020.note: My recount gives 17 on the ratified basis: 9 men's (5000, 10000, marathon, 110H, 400H Warholm 2021, steeplechase, pole vault, shot put, discus) and 8 women's. Unchanged if the pending dos Santos 45.80 and Russell 12.09 (27 Aug 2026) are counted, since they replace 2021 and 2022 records.

records-since-2023.note: My recount gives 12 counting ratified records only (6 men, 6 women). WARNING: Wikipedia lists two pending records from 27 Aug 2026, dos Santos 400H 45.80 (replaces Warholm 2021) and Russell 100H 12.09 (replaces Amusan 2022). Counting them makes it 14. I checked the other 2026 men's rows; none affects this set.

median-year.note: I sorted the 40 years myself: positions 1 to 9 are pre-1990, then 1991, 1993, 1995, 1996, 1998, 2008 and three 2009s (to 18), 2012 (19), then 2016 twice (20 and 21: men's 400 m and women's hammer). The median is 2016. Unchanged if the pending 2026 marks are counted.

m100-1968-year.note: Row: Jim Hines, Mexico City, 14 October 1968.

mmar-first-mark.note: Source row: 2:55:18.4, Johnny Hayes, July 24, 1908, London Olympics. Clock notation converted: 2:55:18.4 (h:mm:ss) = 7200+3300+18.4 = 10518.4 s. This is the first entry in the men's table.

mmar-first-year.note: Hayes row dated July 24, 1908, London Olympics. It is the first row of the men's progression.

mmar-1967-mark.note: Source row: 2:09:36.4, Derek Clayton, December 3, 1967, Fukuoka Marathon. Converted: 2:09:36.4 = 7200+540+36.4 = 7776.4 s.

mmar-kiptum-mark.note: WA 06 Feb 2024 release, verbatim: '2:00:35 Kelvin Kiptum (KEN) Chicago 8 October 2023'. Converted: 2:00:35 = 7200+35 = 7235 s.

mmar-kipchoge-2022-mark.note: WA release: 'world record of 2:01:09 set by his compatriot Eliud Kipchoge in Berlin on 25 September 2022'. Converted: 2:01:09 = 7200+60+9 = 7269 s.

mmar-kipchoge-exhibition-mark.note: The WA Sawe report does say '1:59:41 exhibition performance from 2019'. The widely reported official time is 1:59:40.2 (Vienna, 12 Oct 2019), which is 7180.2 s, or 1:59:40 as usually cited. That falls outside the claim's +/-0.5 s. WA's 41 looks like the road-race round-up convention. Viewers know it as 1:59:40, so say 1:59:40.

mmile-mark.note: Row still present: '3:43.13 ... Hicham El Guerrouj | MAR | 7 Jul 1999 | Golden Gala | Rome'. Kerr's 3:42.66 now tops the mile row as pending, so El Guerrouj stays the ratified record. Converted: 3:43.13 = 223.13 s.

mmile-year.note: El Guerrouj row dated 7 Jul 1999, Golden Gala, Rome. The WA Kerr report ('set 27 years ago') and the WA 1999 report agree.

pending-m400h-mark.note: Quote verified verbatim in the WA 27 Aug 2026 report: 45.80, taking 0.14 off Warholm's 2021 Tokyo record. Wikipedia lists it as pending. This page has no ratification footnote.

pending-w100h-mark.note: Quote verified verbatim: 'Russell stopped the clock at 12.09 to take 0.03 off the previous world record' (Amusan 12.12). Pending status not checked separately: it is not among the records in WA's 3 Sep 2026 ratification release.

pending-mhalf-mark.note: WA: 'clocking 56:51 at the Media Maraton Ciudad de Buenos Aires on 23 August ... Kejelcha's 56:51 is subject to the usual ratification procedure.' Converted: 56:51 = 3360+51 = 3411 s.

shoe-rule-year.note: Release dated 31 Jan 2020. The supplied quote covers retail availability only. The limits themselves are in the release: 'The sole must be no thicker than 40mm' and 'not more than one rigid embedded plate'. The word 'first' is not in the source, so it is unsourced wording.

shoe-rule-sole-mm.note: Verbatim: 'The sole must be no thicker than 40mm.' Release dated 31 January 2020.

shoe-rule-plates.note: Verbatim: 'The shoe must not contain more than one rigid embedded plate or blade (of any material)...'

shoe-rule-retail-months.note: Verbatim: 'From 30 April 2020, any shoe must have been available for purchase ... for a period of four months before it can be used in competition.'

vaporfly-retail-year.note: Quote found verbatim (Complex, 18 Jul 2017). It is a pre-release announcement ('will release on July 20'), not confirmation that the shoe went on sale that day. The year 2017 holds either way.

citius-forecast-year.note: Verbatim: 'half of all WR will not be improved by more than 0,05% in 2027'. Also: 'By 2027, half of the records will reach 99.95% of their asymptotic value, within a [2002-2120] credibility interval.' The interval is wide.

citius-forecast-threshold.note: Verbatim: 'not be improved by more than 0,05% in 2027' (decimal comma in the source).

citius-asymptote-share-2027.note: Verbatim: 'By 2027, half of the records will reach 99.95% of their asymptotic value, within a [2002-2120] credibility interval.'

citius-records-analysed.note: Quote is in Materials and Methods, not the abstract, where the abstract also says 3263 WR. The paper says 'Data were gathered from 1896 to 2007'.

citius-events-analysed.note: Quote found verbatim in Materials and Methods: 147 measurable Olympic events from five disciplines.

citius-start-share-1896.note: Verbatim: 'Starting at 75% of their estimated asymptotic values in 1896'.

citius-share-2008.note: Verbatim: 'WR have now reached 99%'. 'Now' refers to the paper's data, which covers 1896 to 2007.

citius-publication-year.note: Citation: Berthelot G et al. (2008) PLoS ONE 3(2): e1552, published February 6, 2008.
